paragraphs.en: Staring at the {bookcase} in my study, {packed} with so many great books that had {remain} {unread} , I {hear} a {loud} voice in my head—“ {shame} on you! How can you leave these {masterpiece} unread?”
paragraphs.cn: 我凝视着书房里的 <u> 书柜 </u> ，里面 <u> 摆满 </u> 了许多 <u> 还未读过 </u> 的好书，我 <u> 听到 </u> 脑海中有一个 <u> 响亮的 </u> 声音——“真 <u> 丢脸 </u> ！你怎么能把这些 <u> 杰作 </u> 搁置在一旁不读呢？”

paragraphs.en: The first book I picked up was Montaigne's Essays .To my {surprise} I discovered in the margins （页边空白） what clearly was my own {fade} {handwriting} .So I was actually reading it again, but what I was rereading seemed {entirely} new.I also found {sentence} {underline} .Only this time I wondered: Why did I underline this sentence? It's the next one that is important!
paragraphs.cn: 我拿起的第一本书是《蒙田随笔》。令我 <u> 惊讶 </u> 的是，我在页边空白处发现了显然是我自己的 <u> 褪色的笔迹 </u> 。所以我实际上是在重读这本书，但重读的内容似乎是 <u> 全 </u> 新的。我还发现了一些 <u> 画线的句子 </u> 。不过这次我感到疑惑：我为什么要给这句话画线呢？明明下一句话才重要！

paragraphs.en: Clearly, my way of reading the text had shifted, and I {myself} had changed over the years.This raised the larger question of rereading.It comes in many {form}.There's {voluntary} rereading, the result of a {willful} decision to {revisit} a book one has {admire}, or a book that has left one with some {unanswered} questions.This kind of planned revisit could also be for {confirm} certain details in the text, or for checking on the {move} of a given character.A devoted teacher might also {wish} to {refresh} his {closeness} to a work, and thus avoid teaching through the same {old} written notes with soporific （让人瞌睡的） effects.
paragraphs.cn: 显然，我阅读文本的方式发生了变化，而 <u> 我自己 </u> 这些年也变了。这让我想到了关于重读的更重要的问题。重读有多种 <u> 形式 </u> 。一种是 <u> 主动 </u> 重读，是 <u> 有意 </u> 决定 <u> 重读 </u> 一本自己 <u> 欣赏 </u> 的书，或是一本给自己留下 <u> 悬而未决的 </u> 问题的书。这种有计划的重读也可能是为了 <u> 确认 </u> 文中的某些细节，或者是为了核实某个人物的 <u> 行动 </u> 轨迹。一位负责敬业的老师也可能 <u> 希望重新找回 </u> 与某部作品的 <u> 亲近感 </u> ，从而避免照着那些令人昏昏欲睡的 <u> 老旧 </u> 笔记来授课。

paragraphs.en: {contrarily}, there's involuntary rereading.The original reading was {either} forgotten or so {totally} absorbed that the new chance {encounter} with the text produced surprise and {astonishment}.My {reaction} to the {renewed} reading no longer {correspond} to the original experience, and I was no longer sure that I recognized myself as the same reader.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 相反地 </u> ，也有非自愿重读。初次阅读的内容 <u> 要么 </u> 已被遗忘，要么被 <u> 彻底 </u> 吸收，以至于再次 <u> 偶然遇到 </u> 这段文字时，会产生惊讶和 <u> 诧异 </u> 的感觉。我 <u> 重 </u> 读的 <u> 反应 </u> 不再与初次阅读时的体验 <u> 相符 </u> ，我甚至不再确定自己是否还是当初那个读者。

paragraphs.en: Then there are what one might call subconscious （潜意识的） rereadings, those that {occur} {without} the {specific} act of reading, much as the {memory} of a {tune} can keep coming back to the mind without its actually being heard again.This form of remembered {contact} with a book can {accompany} us {during} a {lifetime} and continue to {strengthen} and {shape} us.Much in the same {manner}, we may over the years recite to ourselves poems learned by heart long ago, which have become part of our self-recognition.
paragraphs.cn: 还有一种重读可能被称为“潜意识的重读”，这种重读并 <u> 不 </u> 通过 <u> 具体的 </u> 阅读行为来 <u> 实现 </u> ，非常像对一段 <u> 曲调 </u> 的 <u> 记忆 </u> 不断在脑海中回响，而实际上并没有再听到这首曲子一样。这种与书的记忆式 <u> 接触 </u> 会 <u> 伴随 </u> 我们 <u> 一生 </u> ，并持续地 <u> 塑造 </u> 我们，让我们得到 <u> 提升 </u> 。同 <u> 样 </u> ，我们也可以长年累月背诵很久以前就熟记的诗歌，这些诗歌已经成为我们自我认知的一部分。

paragraphs.en: All of these ways of reading are {valuable}.Renewed contact with a novel or a poem can {activate} the {search} for a better {knowledge} of the self.The new reading, a form of revision, {uncover} the change in us.The {newness} is not in the text.It is we who have {evolve}.In the process of rereading, our {outlook} has also been significantly changed.Rereading makes it possible for us to see the world around us, ourselves included, in a new {light}.
paragraphs.cn: 所有这些阅读方式都是 <u> 有价值的 </u> 。重新与一部小说或一首诗歌接触，能够 <u> 激发 </u> 我们去 <u> 探索 </u> 自我，对自己有更深入的 <u> 了解 </u> 。这种新的阅读，作为一种重温的方式， <u> 揭示 </u> 了我们自身的变化。 <u> 新意 </u> 并不在于文本本身，而在于我们自身的 <u> 成长 </u> 。在重读的过程中，我们的 <u> 观念 </u> 也发生了明显变化。重读使我们能够以新的 <u> 视角 </u> 看待周围的世界，包括我们自己。
